correctness.rationale: The proof reconstructs from the frozen RESULT.md. Writing the derivation as the commuting sum of the shear derivation and minus the inner derivation by \(g(y)\), the top \(x\)-degree term of a kernel element must centralize nonconstant \(g(y)\); the free-algebra centralizer theorem therefore forces the kernel to be \(k[y]\). For nonconstant \(g\), repeated application to \(x\) produces nonzero iterated commutators with strictly growing word degree, excluding local nilpotence and local finiteness; scalar \(g\) leaves an elementary locally nilpotent shear. Any commuting automorphism preserves the kernel, hence sends \(y\) affinely; the rank-two automorphism theorem then makes \(x\) triangular. Substitution gives exactly \(g(ay+b)-g(y)\in k\) and \(f(ay+b)=cf(y)\), from which the stated residual cyclic symmetry follows.
